subject: Solstice security checkpoint & log-sample handoff
messages:
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@solsticeanalytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Gina Park <gina.park@solsticeanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Quick sync + log sample request for CAIQ answers

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

Thanks again for the earlier intro. We're running through the CAIQ and have two quick asks before our internal review on Friday: 1) a short window to confirm how Redwood handles ephemeral logs for hosted API requests, and 2) a small anonymized log sample (just headers + timing metadata) to validate retention/rotation behavior.

Would you be available for a 30-minute checkpoint tomorrow afternoon? Our preferred windows: 2027-05-05 11:00-12:30 PT or 2027-05-05 14:00-16:00 PT. If neither work, propose alternatives. Also, can you confirm the file format you can share for the log sample and whether any redaction steps are required on your side?

We appreciate a short action list we can bring to our review.

Best,
Alex
Alex Wu
Security Lead
Solstice Analytics

--
Attachment references: none in this message
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@solsticeanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick sync + log sample request for CAIQ answers

Thanks Alex — available to run through this. Proposed plan:

- Quick 30-min checkpoint to explain log retention, sampling, and redaction.
- We can provide a CSV of anonymized metadata (timestamp, request_id, model_id, token_count, region) with all PII stripped.
- We'll include a short architecture diagram showing where ephemeral logs are buffered and how long cached KV and request traces are retained.

Proposed times (all PT):
- 2027-05-05 11:30 - 12:00
- 2027-05-05 14:30 - 15:00

Action items if we meet:
1) We'll upload a redacted log-sample CSV to a shared Drive link right after the call.
2) Kimberly will confirm whether the sample needs any extra HMAC or blinding for your audit team.
3) I'll drop the SOC 2 architecture PDF into the Drive folder.

If you prefer, we can also do a quick recorded demo of the log-export workflow.

Jonas Weber
Head of Solutions
Redwood Inference

--

Jonas — great, 11:30-12:00 PT works for us.

Two quick clarifications before the call:
- For the log-sample CSV, we only need the metadata columns you listed; please remove any x-forwarded-for or IP fields. Anonymized request_id is fine.
- On the architecture PDF, could you include a brief note about which components are customer-data-in-scope vs. telemetry-only? That helps our evidence mapping.

Confirming the 11:30 PT time and we'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Alex

Hi Alex / Gina — thanks for the call earlier. Per the meeting notes: 

- Attached is the redacted log sample (redwood-log-sample-manifest.csv) and SOC 2 architecture diagram (redwood-soc2-architecture-diagram.pdf). Both are uploaded to the shared Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cSolsticeEvidence
- The CSV contains only timestamp, request_id (anonymized), model_id, token_count, and region. No IPs or user identifiers.
- Kimberly confirmed we do not need to HMAC the sample for your internal review. If you require extra blinding, let us know and we can produce a second variant.
